title: Downtown Brownsville host mixer over infrastructure, revitalization plans - NewsBreak
text:
By Shirley Escobedo ,
1 hours ago
BROWNSVILLE, Texas ( ValleyCentral ) — A Master Plan Revitalization mixer was hosted in Downtown Brownsville Wednesday afternoon to discuss future plans about revitalization, funding, phasing and priorities.
City of Brownsville Assistant City Manager, Doroteo Garcia Jr., spoke about some of the major street reconstruction projects that the Institute for Leadership in Capital Projects is bringing together.
Damage to your vehicle due to road construction: Here’s how to file a claim “We have several roadway reconstruction projects consisting of Coffee Port Road and Old Highway 77. We’ll be starting on Old Alice, and Coffee Port will have a second phase from Paredes Line Road to Port Isabel Road and 14th Street,” Garcia said. “Then we have a lot of park improvements that we’re doing in collaboration with BCIC as well. The park improvements range from several splash pads, playground innovations, and numerous improvements to the existing facilities that we have, which is what our community is looking for.
Garcia also said several public sessions regarding The Downtown Master Plan have been completed, and it’s close to being presented to the public.
Some of the presentations include shaded walkways, parking, and congregation areas similar to the Market Square.
Brownsville man charged with pulling out a gun during a fight Garcia added that a lot of roadway construction and detours are expected while these projects are underway.
Therefore, Brownsville residents are asked to be patient, be cautious while driving, stay off cell phones, and be alert on the road.
Those not from Brownsville are invited to come check out what is being built.
